beats.intent: ThinkSR turns a low-resolution image into windows, repeatedly updates them with shared DQ-CTM ticks, then decodes the dense result.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: ThinkSR keeps the dense carrier outside the compact thought process. The encoder starts from the low-resolution image. Windowing groups the dense field without dropping tokens. The DQ-CTM thought process runs recurrent ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR recurs inside the thought stage, not around the whole model
params.note: The recurrence belongs to the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features, and window partitioning creates the token sequence while preserving the dense field.
beats.narration: The carrier equation defines the dense representation before thought begins. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window operator partitions that field into tokens while keeping the carrier intact.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first, then partitioned into windows

terms.label: encoder turns the low-resolution image into features

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; its 1.129 million parameters rank second largest among the five methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should not be read as a cheap-model result. CATANet is the smallest at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN and IMDN also stay below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR uses 1.129 million parameters, the second largest count here. CARN is larger at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest model in this comparison
